sections.label: Patent law amendments proposed
sections.summary: The passage states three changes: broadening the grace period, closing the foreign route, and implementing procedural amendments for applicants and IPOS efficiency.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: First, we will broaden the grace period provision to better allow inventors to protect their inventions, while facilitating the spread of new ideas and technologies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Second, we will close the foreign route to obtaining a patent in Singapore to improve the quality and consistency of granted patents.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Third, we will implement procedural amendments to allow applicants greater flexibility in the application process and to improve operational efficiency at the Intellectual Property Office of Singapore (IPOS).

sections.label: Closing foreign examination route
sections.summary: The passage states that applicants were once allowed to rely on foreign examination reports, and this route is now proposed to be closed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: However, at that point of time, we allowed patent applicants to rely on foreign examination reports for the same invention to enter our system.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We are now proposing to close this route so that all patent applications are fully examined by our examiners against our standards of patentability.

sections.label: Clause 3(a) closes foreign route
sections.summary: The passage states clause 3(a) closes the foreign route, requiring local or mixed routes and full examination under Singapore's laws.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Clause 3(a) of the present Bill, therefore, closes the foreign route option.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For patent applications filed on or after the prescribed date, they must go through either the local or mixed route.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Patents will be granted only after full examination based on Singapore's laws and practices.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This will, therefore, ensure the quality of Singapore granted patents and increase stakeholders' confidence in the validity of these patents.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This amendment aligns our patent system with that of major jurisdictions, such as the US, Japan and Europe, which do not provide for the foreign route mechanism and require all patent applications to be fully examined by their patent offices.

sections.label: Bill aims and foreign route
sections.summary: The passage states the Bill seeks to ensure high patent standards by closing the foreign route and to broaden the grace period for novelty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: These steps have allowed us to enhance our IP regulatory framework even further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This Bill broadly seeks to: (a) ensure the high standard of Singapore's patents by the closure of the foreign route; and (b) broaden the grace period for the determination of novelty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Under that foreign route, Singapore relies on the search and examination report of other countries and does a supplementary examination.

sections.label: Clause 2 broadens grace period
sections.summary: The passage states that clause 2 of the Bill seeks to broaden the grace period for the determination of novelty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The second amendment is to be found in clause 2 of this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: That clause seeks to broaden the grace period for the determination of novelty.

sections.label: Innovation safe space and masterplan
sections.summary: The passage states this gives innovators a safe space to seek funding without compromising protection, and a revised IP Hub Masterplan will be released in April.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This gives innovation a safe space in which innovators can seek funding without compromising the protection of their inventions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It has been reported that the revised IP Hub Masterplan that caters to entrepreneurship and innovation will be released in April.

sections.label: Patent amendments and grace period
sections.summary: The Bill discontinues supplementary examination, requires examination in Singapore, and broadens the 12-month grace period for novelty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I rise in support of these amendments which balance strengthening the IP rights regime which encourages investment in research and development and innovation, while recognising that excessive protection of products or services that are not truly novel can hinder innovation and entrepreneurship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This Bill discontinues the supplementary examination route and requires at least the examination to be done in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This creates a more rigorous check on the quality of patents and ensures that successful patents are truly deserving of legal protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I also welcome the new section 14(4)(e) which broadens the 12-month "grace period" exception to determining whether an invention is novel, as this takes into account business needs and practical realities.

sections.label: Disclosure wording and common law
sections.summary: The member asks whether section 14(4)(e) differs substantively on disclosure and whether common law disclosure understanding is retained.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Minister of State clarify if there is any substantive difference in terms of what amounts to disclosure between the wording in section 14(4)(a) to (d), and that of 14(4)(e)?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Do we retain the common law understanding that disclosure even to one person not under an obligation of confidence constitutes disclosure to the public?

sections.label: IPOS patent office arrangements
sections.summary: IPOS has arrangements with patent offices worldwide letting applicants use a Singapore examination report to expedite applications elsewhere.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: IPOS has arrangements with patent offices around the world to allow applicants to use a Singapore patent examination report to expedite applications in other jurisdictions.

sections.label: Search and examination fee decrease
sections.summary: The fee for requesting a search and examination report will decrease by 25% from 1 April.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The fee for requesting a search and examination report will decrease by 25% with effect from 1 April.

sections.label: IP master's and examiners
sections.summary: IPOS and UniSIM announced a Master in IP and Innovation Management, and IPOS' patent unit has over 100 examiners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In this regard, IPOS and the Singapore Institute of Management (UniSIM) have announced the launch of a Master in IP and Innovation Management this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Second, IPOS' patent search and examination unit has more than 100 examiners with expertise across a wide range of technologies.
